boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Trinity University customs, campus legends, and recurring celebrations in San Antonio.

cards.title: Begin with First Fiesta
cards.subtitle: New Tiger Orientation
cards.notes: Look for this orientation gathering, where the president invites new students to her home for a celebration of community and San Antonio culture.
cards.short_summary: A presidential welcome tradition during New Tiger Orientation.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity identifies First Fiesta as a New Tiger Orientation celebration hosted at the president’s home.
cards.source_title: Campus Community and Traditions | Trinity University
cards.access_notes: For incoming students during New Tiger Orientation; participation details vary by year.

cards.title: Christmas Vespers by Candlelight
cards.subtitle: Parker Chapel
cards.notes: Attend the annual candlelight service in Parker Chapel, then continue into the accompanying Christmas on Oakmont gathering if it is offered.
cards.short_summary: A yearly service of carols and candlelight in Parker Chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity lists Christmas Vespers as an annual candlelight service in Parker Chapel followed by Christmas on Oakmont.
cards.source_title: Campus Community and Traditions | Trinity University
cards.access_notes: Annual holiday event; consult the university events calendar for the current date and attendance details.

cards.title: Follow Vespers to Oakmont
cards.subtitle: Oakmont Court
cards.notes: After Christmas Vespers, visit the open houses on Oakmont Court for holiday cheer with the Trinity community when scheduled.
cards.short_summary: Holiday open houses that follow Trinity’s Vespers service.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity describes Christmas on Oakmont as holiday open houses on Oakmont following Christmas Vespers.
cards.source_title: Campus Community and Traditions | Trinity University
cards.access_notes: Held in connection with annual Christmas Vespers; confirm current arrangements before attending.

cards.title: Watch the Class Rings Arrive
cards.subtitle: Murchison Tower and Miller Fountain
cards.notes: If you are eligible for a class ring, follow the ceremony’s current instructions and enjoy the campus spectacle surrounding the ring presentation.
cards.short_summary: A class-ring presentation tied to Murchison Tower and Miller Fountain.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity says class rings are brought down from Murchison Tower and presented during its Ring Ceremony.
cards.source_title: Campus Community and Traditions | Trinity University
cards.access_notes: Participation is tied to receiving a class ring; follow event staff directions and current ceremony guidance.

cards.title: Study by the Magic Stones
cards.subtitle: Campus study legend
cards.notes: Make the stones a pre-exam study stop, then rely on your preparation; Trinity presents the good-luck effect as a campus legend.
cards.short_summary: A study superstition promising luck on the next exam.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity says campus legend holds that studying by the Magic Stones brings good luck on the next exam.
cards.source_title: Campus Community and Traditions | Trinity University
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; use normal campus access rules.

cards.title: Rub LeeRoy’s Nose
cards.subtitle: LeeRoy tiger statue
cards.notes: Pause at the LeeRoy statue before a Tiger contest and rub its nose for luck, keeping the mascot legend in its playful context.
cards.short_summary: A luck ritual centered on Trinity’s LeeRoy tiger statue.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity describes rubbing the nose of its LeeRoy statue as a good-luck tradition for the Tiger team.
cards.source_title: Campus Community and Traditions | Trinity University
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus statue; observe posted campus rules and avoid damaging the sculpture.

cards.title: Mind the Northrup Hall Seal
cards.subtitle: Northrup Hall
cards.notes: Notice the seal at Northrup Hall and decide whether to honor the graduation superstition by giving it a wide berth on your walk.
cards.short_summary: A campus superstition about stepping on the Northrup Hall seal.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity reports a campus rumor that students who walk on the Northrup Hall seal will not graduate in four years.
cards.source_title: Campus Community and Traditions | Trinity University
cards.access_notes: Accessible as part of normal campus circulation; the stated consequence is presented by Trinity as rumor.

cards.title: Cheer During Hallympics
cards.subtitle: Residence hall competitions
cards.notes: Support your residence hall in the Residential Life competitions held near the beginning of the academic year, following current event rules.
cards.short_summary: Residential Life’s annual inter-hall competition series.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity says Residential Life sponsors Hallympics competitions between residence halls at the beginning of each academic year.
cards.source_title: Campus Community and Traditions | Trinity University
cards.access_notes: Residential Life event; schedules, events, and eligibility are set annually.

cards.title: Catch a 12:22 Happy Friday Set
cards.subtitle: Coates Student Center lobby
cards.notes: Stop by the Coates Student Center lobby at 12:22 p.m. on an announced Friday to hear the AcaBellas or Trinitones perform.
cards.short_summary: A recurring midday a cappella performance tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity says the AcaBellas and Trinitones alternate Happy Friday performances at 12:22 p.m. on most fall and spring Fridays.
cards.source_title: Campus Community and Traditions | Trinity University
cards.access_notes: Occurs on most Fridays during fall and spring semesters; verify the current schedule before going.

cards.title: See Spotlight’s Student Acts
cards.subtitle: Annual student talent show
cards.notes: Attend Trinity’s annual student talent show to see performers share skills ranging from music and dance to other stage acts.
cards.short_summary: An annual showcase for Trinity student performers.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity identifies Spotlight as its annual student talent show showcasing skills and abilities across campus.
cards.source_title: Campus Community and Traditions | Trinity University
cards.access_notes: Annual event; consult the university events calendar for current venue, admission, and participation details.
